titleZh: 数值、单位、变量与表达式
title: Numbers, units, variables, and expressions

blocks.text: The previous chapter saved a hand calculation as a program. This chapter asks what a value represents, why the same number with a different unit becomes a different quantity, how evaluation order is determined, and why a measurement is not an exact truth. Every example still uses basic arithmetic and Python syntax already introduced.

blocks.caption: 单位尺度图的阅读任务：先确认对象和尺度，再进行换算。

blocks.text: You will write a unit-bearing physical quantity as a checkable expression and state the boundary of measurement precision.
2.1 A number is not a quantity

blocks.right: 数字 + 单位 + 对象
blocks.note: 在机器人中还常要补充方向、坐标系和时间。 / Robotics often also needs direction, frame, and time.

blocks.text: The number 7 is only a value. 7 mm, 7 cm, 7 s, and 7 kg describe different kinds of quantities. A quantity contains at least a value and a unit; robot systems often also require an object, direction, frame, and time. We begin by making values and units explicit.

blocks.title: 同一个7为什么不能直接相加 / Why two sevens may not be added

blocks.text: A blade datum has an error of 7 mm and the robot waits for 7 s. The arithmetic $7+7=14$ is valid, but “14 millimetre-seconds” answers no sensible question. Addition requires quantities of the same kind with compatible units.

blocks.title: 量纲与单位 / Dimension and unit

blocks.text: A dimension describes a kind of quantity, such as length, time, or mass. A unit gives the scale used to measure it, such as metres, centimetres, or millimetres for length. 2 m and 200 cm have different numerical values but the same length; 2 m and 2 s share a value but are different kinds of quantities.
2.2 Unit conversion multiplies by a ratio equal to one
Since $1\ \mathrm{m}=1000\ \mathrm{mm}$, the ratio $1\ \mathrm{m}/1000\ \mathrm{mm}$ divides one length by the same length and therefore equals one. Converting 35 mm to metres can be written as

Millimetres cancel between numerator and denominator, leaving metres. This is safer than memorising “divide by 1000,” because a reversed conversion becomes visible in the units. To convert 0.035 m back to millimetres, use the reciprocal ratio.

blocks.code:
offset_mm = 35
offset_m = offset_mm / 1000
recovered_mm = offset_m * 1000

assert offset_m == 0.035
assert recovered_mm == offset_mm
print(offset_m)

blocks.text: A round-trip check converts from A to B and back to A, then checks whether the original value is recovered. It does not prove all unit logic, but catches many direction and scale errors.
2.3 Integers and decimal numbers

Python uses different types for different kinds of data. `35` is an integer and `0.035` is a floating-point number. Floating-point values approximate real numbers with decimals. Later numerical-computing chapters explain their representation; for now, know that some decimal fractions cannot be stored exactly in binary.

`abs` computes absolute value. The check asks whether the difference is smaller than $10^{-12}$ rather than requiring exact equality. A tolerance must not be chosen arbitrarily large; it should be stricter than the task error allowance and appropriate to the scale.
2.4 Evaluation order in an expression

The expression $2+3\times4$ evaluates multiplication first and gives 14, whereas $(2+3)\times4$ gives 20. Python uses the same basic precedence. Even when precedence is known, parentheses should expose the intended structure in unit conversions, averages, and error formulas.

blocks.title: 平均值中的括号 / Parentheses in an average

blocks.text: Three measurements are 10.1, 9.9, and 10.0 mm. Their mean is $(10.1+9.9+10.0)/3=10.0$ mm. Writing `10.1 + 9.9 + 10.0 / 3` divides only the final value by three and no longer computes the mean.

blocks.code:
measurement_1_mm = 10.1
measurement_2_mm = 9.9
measurement_3_mm = 10.0

mean_mm = (
    measurement_1_mm + measurement_2_mm + measurement_3_mm
) / 3
assert abs(mean_mm - 10.0) < 1e-12

blocks.text: 2.5 Variables change with execution order

The mathematical equation $x=x+1$ cannot hold for an ordinary real number, because subtraction would give $0=1$. In Python, `x = x + 1` is not an equation: it reads the old value, adds one, and associates `x` with the new value.

blocks.code:
sample_count = 0
sample_count = sample_count + 1
sample_count = sample_count + 1
assert sample_count == 2

blocks.text: This allows a program to record state, but means code cannot be read without execution order. Loops later repeat such updates; robot state, training steps, and experiment counts all use this mechanism.
2.6 A measurement is not an exact truth

blocks.note: 最后一位数字必须与仪器分辨率相称。 / The final digit must match instrument resolution.

blocks.text: Reading 35 mm from a ruler with 1 mm divisions does not imply that the true length is exactly $35.000\ldots$ mm. The reading depends on resolution, viewing angle, placement, and operator. A measurement record should contain at least a value, unit, and measurement condition.

blocks.title: 误差、不确定性与容差先做区分 / First distinction among error, uncertainty, and tolerance

blocks.text: Error commonly means the difference between a measurement or estimate and a reference. Uncertainty describes limited knowledge of a value. Tolerance is the deviation allowed by a task. They are related but not identical. This chapter establishes the distinction; probability and statistics chapters provide formal methods.

If blade assembly allows 0.02 mm of position error while the measuring tool reliably resolves only 1 mm, adding decimal places does not solve the problem. `35.000000` looks more precise but contains no additional measurement information.
2.7 A minimal measurement program

blocks.caption: 单位、平均值和容差的最小实验 / Minimal experiment with units, mean, and tolerance
blocks.code:
"""Minimal measurement experiment for Chapter 2."""

measurement_1_mm = 10.1
measurement_2_mm = 9.9
measurement_3_mm = 10.0

mean_mm = (
    measurement_1_mm + measurement_2_mm + measurement_3_mm
) / 3

target_mm = 10.0
tolerance_mm = 0.2
absolute_error_mm = abs(mean_mm - target_mm)
within_tolerance = absolute_error_mm <= tolerance_mm

assert abs(mean_mm - 10.0) < 1e-12
assert absolute_error_mm < 1e-12
assert within_tolerance

print(mean_mm)
print(absolute_error_mm)
print(within_tolerance)

blocks.text: The program preserves the unit of three readings, computes their mean, and compares the absolute difference from a target. The Boolean value `within_tolerance` is either `True` or `False`; the next chapter formally introduces comparisons and Booleans. For now, predict the three printed results and compare them with the run.

blocks.title: 单位一致，测量仍可能无效 / Compatible units do not guarantee a valid measurement

blocks.text: All three readings may come from the same uncalibrated ruler, producing a stable mean with a common offset. Repetition reveals random variation but does not automatically remove systematic bias. Later statistics chapters separate random and systematic error.

blocks.text: These cases establish only the shared principle that a value needs semantics. Navigation, torque, and neural networks are not prerequisites here. When each topic is introduced, we return to the same table with additional mathematics and code.
